stem: A client with severe untreated hypothyroidism develops hypothermia, bradycardia, and a markedly decreased level of consciousness. Which complication is most likely?
rationale: NCBI/StatPearls describes myxedema coma as the severe, life-threatening manifestation of hypothyroidism characterized by altered mentation and multiorgan dysfunction; common findings include hypothermia and bradycardia. In a client with severe untreated hypothyroidism, the combination of hypothermia, bradycardia and markedly decreased consciousness therefore most strongly supports myxedema coma. Thyroid storm produces severe thyrotoxicosis rather than this hypothyroid pattern; adrenal crisis and sepsis do not best explain the full constellation.
educational_objective: Recognize the classic decompensated hypothyroid presentation of myxedema coma.
source_locator: Introduction; History and Physical; Evaluation — altered mental status and hypothermia are common/core findings; bradycardia is a common associated finding.
source_claim_supported: Severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia and altered consciousness is characteristic of myxedema coma.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — acute/complex alterations and endocrine emergencies.

source_original.stem: A client with severe untreated hypothyroidism develops hypothermia, bradycardia, and a markedly decreased level of consciousness. Which complication is most likely?
source_original.rationale: Severe decompensated hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, and major alteration in mental status is characteristic of myxedema coma, so Option B is correct. Adrenal crisis and septic shock can cause hemodynamic instability but do not specifically match this severe hypothyroid pattern. Thyroid storm is severe thyrotoxicosis and typically produces the opposite hyperadrenergic pattern.
source_original.source_detail: StatPearls Myxedema Coma — History and Physical/Evaluation: decompensated severe hypothyroidism typically features altered mental status and hypothermia, with bradycardia, hypotension or hypoventilation and multisystem dysfunction; it is a life-threatening endocrine emergency. StatPearls Myxedema Coma updated 2025-12-13 and current in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
